hn-50305693.t: AI isn't replacing SREs, it's deskilling them
hn-50305693.s: When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters?
ex: There are two popular prophecies floating around tech circles these days. The first says SRE is the future of all software engineering, that as AI writes more and more code, the humans who remain will be the ones keeping systems alive. The second says AI will devour every tech job alive, SREs included. Neither is particularly useful if you’re an SRE trying to figure out what your Tuesday will look like in 2027. Let’s ask a more grounded question by looking at what’s already happening: When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters? Most of us already use AI for our daily work (our brains a little fried!), and so do SREs. Today’s discussion agenda is not whether AI replaces SREs, but whether AI is quietly making SREs less capable and whether anyone will notice anything before the next novel outage hits. The foundational framework for this entire debate comes from a 1983 research paper that’s eerily prescient.

hn-50306442.t: A working Nintendo in ~1GB of Qwen weights
hn-50306442.s: An NES CPU compiled into the weights of a stock Qwen3.5 model
ex: An NES CPU compiled into the weights of a stock Qwen3.5 model. The NES's 6502 CPU (the core of its 2A03 chip), its 2 KB of work RAM, and a cartridge's program ROM run inside a standard Qwen35ForCausalLM checkpoint. Nobody trained these weights; a compiler computed every one. When you play a game, the model predicts the CPU's execution log one token at a time. A small host program plays the rest of the console around it: it draws the picture, reads the controller, and fires the vblank interrupt. nesformer builds on Qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, which compiled a CHIP-8 and then a RISC-V CPU into Qwen3.5-4B. It reuses Qwenputer's compiler and its central trick: the model's Gated DeltaNet state is the machine's memory. Every CPU token in these runs came from the model. For the bundled test games, every frame also matches a conventional 6502 emulator's output exactly (see How it was checked). Unzip nesformer.zip and nesformer-weights.zip into the same folder.

hn-50305573.s: For most of the past two decades, the code forge has been where projects live: where code is hosted, where changes are reviewed, and where contributors find each other.
ex: For most of the past two decades, the code forge has been where projects live: where code is hosted, where changes are reviewed, and where contributors find each other. Forges offered convenience in exchange for centralisation. But the centralised forge is crumbling. Relying on someone else for uptime, for features, and to be a good steward of your code hasn’t played out well. What has stood the test of time is email: Git to move the code, and email — an open protocol — to talk about it. At the cost of user experience, however. Tangled aims to give you the best of both: the longevity of an open protocol, with the convenience and polish of a proper forge. It’s the first truly federated code forge — you can host code on your own servers and still collaborate seamlessly with others. Our approach is pragmatic: self-host just the parts you want, like Git hosting or CI runners, or all of it, including the API server and UI. Whatever you choose, you can still talk to everyone else.

hn-50295450.t: A tiny world model running games on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
hn-50295450.s: Tiny world model generates games and stream ac plays them all on Pico 2W
ex: Using 2 small neural networks to generate and play the game at the same time on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. The first one creates the game: given the current frame and the action, it predicts the next frame and the reward. The second one plays that game: it uses the generated frame and picks an action. Every frame above was sampled by the world model network, and the actions were taken by the actor network. I got interested in looped transformers, where one transformer block is applied several times with the same weights instead of stacking different layers. Reusing weights is cheap on memory, so I wanted to see if a looped world model could be small enough to run on a microcontroller. I picked the Pico 2 W because it is cheap and has an FPU, and small games because I could write the real versions directly into numpy and check every generated frame against them. Later I added a streaming RL agent so the board could also learn to play inside its own dream.

hn-50305637.s: Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LuaLaTeX, drawn in Lua
ex: The Reddit post asked how to make flowers like these in LaTeX. I don't know how the original was made, and this project doesn't try to reproduce it. It is one possible way, and the way I did it: hand-authored primitives with randomized parameters, painted in Lua, placed by a procedural layout whose "fill the unused space" part borrows a 1998 idea from the ornament literature. It gets a similar look. Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LaTeX. No images, no imported paths, no external assets: every petal, leaf and stem is a parametric curve computed in Lua while the page is being written, painted like a watercolor, and written straight into the PDF. Every page gets its own garden. Six seeds of the grown composition. Same code, different seed — and the garden fills whatever space the text leaves free. Two documents share one package, and a third shows what else it does: Both PDFs are self-describing: the body text is the write-up of how the margin is drawn.

hn-50297697.t: I Turned DOOM into a Transformer
hn-50297697.s: Compile an integer neural network into a DOOM map. Voodoo dolls do the arithmetic, light levels and plane heights hold the values, and every value is checked against NumPy with tolerance 0.
ex: doomformer doctor checks your setup. It builds ACC, the ACS compiler, if it is missing. That needs git, cmake and a C compiler. On Fedora: sudo dnf install git cmake gcc gcc-c++ make. The marine holds FIRE and inks the floor. Then he presses READ. 1,355 voodoo dolls in the same map run an MNIST network. The winning digit's doll crosses a line. That line lights the digit on the display. Python reads back 248 values and checks every one. With --digit, Python presses the keys for you. Without it, you walk and draw yourself. Full output The float model scores 97.58 %. The network also trained on the strokes the scripted marine walks. Details · Film Step on seven floor pads to light a digit. Press READ. 136 voodoo dolls run a tiny network and light the answer. Press MUTATE and the level rewires one connection while it runs. The same 7 now reads as 1. You can watch it happen: one doll stops at its gate. A self-test version runs exactly in GZDoom, LZDoom, UZDoom and ZDoom 2.8.1.

hn-50299182.t: CVE-2026-98432: Linux TCP Use-After-Free Risk and Patch Validation
hn-50299182.s: CVE-2026-98432: check Go MPTCP listeners, AWS and Amazon Linux fixes, Proxmox kernels, AlmaLinux status and patch verification after reboot.
ex: CVE-2026-98432 is a use-after-free in the Linux kernel’s IPv4 TCP handshake path. The flaw appears when two processors act on related request and child sockets while both can still reference the same IP options object. One path may free that object immediately while another path, protected only as an RCU reader, continues to use it. The result is a stale kernel pointer in code reachable through network traffic. The Linux CNA record assigns CVSS 3.1 9.8. Distribution assessments must be read against their own products and metric versions; consult the current Red Hat advisory for RHEL rather than applying an upstream score to every distribution. Separately, Anthropic reported remote root command execution against a server with a Multipath TCP listener in a controlled lab. That demonstrates serious exploitability under a specific configuration, not universal compromise of every Linux TCP listener. Defenders should treat those statements as complementary.

hn-50299004.t: Lasm – Write formally verified webapps in Lean for Node/serverless/edge
hn-50299004.s: Lean for JavaScript and WebAssembly runtimes
ex: Lean 4 for the JavaScript and WebAssembly world. Lasm compiles ordinary Lean 4 programs ahead of time to WebAssembly. One Lean code base can become a Node server, a serverless or edge function, a WASI/Fastly module or a browser app. Because it is Lean, you can prove properties of the code you deploy. The flagship example, Conduit, is the RealWorld app with 117 proved theorems. Lasm ships on npm and brings Lean, Lake and its build tools with it; you only need Node (or Bun or Deno). AI agents: this README is complete on its own. llms.txt is the short index, and docs/AI.md lists the rules that save you from wrong turns. If Lasm is useful to you, I'd appreciate your sponsorship (more below). Every row is tested in CI with the platform's own local runtime, image or emulator. By project policy CI never deploys to a real cloud account (how each is tested). Node builds have Lean's full runtime (threads, files, processes, sockets).

hn-50305480.t: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binance
hn-50305480.s: The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange reported Thursday that approximately $6.3 billion was impacted in an apparent hack.
ex: FILE - The Binance logo is seen on a smartphone, Feb. 28, 2023, in Marple Township, Pa. Matt Slocum/AP hide caption A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm says a North Korean unit was likely behind the hack that impacted more than $6 billion on Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange. Binance said it worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets. It said Friday that it was beginning to recover assets for users. The cryptocurrency exchange said deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals have been suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two. It said it will cover all losses. The company said on X that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional "points of breach." TRM, in a post on its website Thursday, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea's elite hacking unit.
